stemMd: In the second paragraph, the author says a model "could therefore give the wrong answer precisely because it was faithful." As used here, "faithful" most nearly means

options.label: A
options.textMd: loyal to the engineers who had designed it.

options.label: B
options.textMd: an exact copy of the river's proportions.

options.label: C
options.textMd: reliable in the predictions it produced.

options.label: D
options.textMd: made of the same materials as the river bed.

options.label: E
options.textMd: used regularly over a long period of time.

explanationMd:
The sentence itself defines the word, just before it is used: "A model built faithfully to one scale in every direction". Being faithful here means reproducing the river's shape exactly, with every dimension shrunk by the same factor. The author's point is a paradox: the more exact the copy, the shallower its water, and very shallow water does not flow like a river.

The most tempting wrong choice is the everyday sense of "faithful" as "reliable". Test it by substitution: a model that "could give the wrong answer precisely because it was reliable" contradicts itself. The other senses, loyalty, same materials, long use, are not about the model's relation to the river's proportions.

distractorRationale.c: Substituted, this gives a model that gives the wrong answer because it is reliable, which contradicts itself. The sentence says the faithful model's answers could be wrong.
distractorRationale.a: Loyalty to people is a familiar sense of "faithful", but the phrase "built faithfully to one scale in every direction" is about the model's relation to the river's shape, not to its designers.
distractorRationale.d: The passage says the real models were made of concrete and later used lighter grains instead of sand; faithfulness here is about scale, not materials.
distractorRationale.e: Nothing in the sentence refers to how long or how often a model was used; the word is tied to being built "to one scale in every direction".

accessibilityText: A meaning-in-context question about the river models passage. It asks what "faithful" most nearly means in the second-paragraph sentence saying a model "could therefore give the wrong answer precisely because it was faithful". The five choices: loyal to the engineers who had designed it; an exact copy of the river's proportions; reliable in the predictions it produced; made of the same materials as the river bed; used regularly over a long period of time.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage; it tests the meaning of a word whose everyday sense would make the sentence contradict itself. Every option is answerable, or refutable, from the passage text alone.

review.author: tolc-i-wave8-verbal-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: 'Built faithfully to one scale in every direction' means an exact proportional copy of the river. 'Reliable in its predictions' is the opposite of the point, since the faithful model gives the wrong answer. Loyalty to its designers, the same materials (the passage says concrete beds and substitute grains) and long use are not meant. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolci-verbal-run1) reached the same answer: 'Built faithfully to one scale in every direction' = an exact proportional copy. 'Reliable in its predictions' contradicts the sentence (it gave the wrong answer); loyal, same materials and long use are irrelevant senses.]
